title: Keep-Right-Except-to-Pass Rule Evaluation and Traffic-Rule Design

limitations: All 40 PDF pages were rendered and visually reviewed.
p1 is the six-paragraph Summary; p2 is decorative title material and p3 is Contents, both excluded from language evidence.
p32 begins References and Appendix; p33-p40 are author C++ retained for reproducibility but excluded from natural-language learning.
Text extraction has mojibake for some mathematical symbols, so all retained equations were checked against rendered pages.

deliverables: Evaluate KRETP by traffic flow, safety proxy, and energy proxy across vehicle densities.
Choose speed limits under light, heavy, and mixed traffic.
Use a continuum representation to corroborate the discrete density-flow pattern and discuss orientation transfer.
Evaluate a median-based intelligent-system control extension and state future centralized-control opportunities.
task_reconstruction.reconstruction_limit: No official problem statement was located with the paper; task wording is reconstructed only from author prose and is not used to classify A-F.

section_map.summary: Six visual paragraphs: policy question -> dual models -> metrics/scope -> alternatives -> median control -> limitations.
Navigation only; excluded from author-language evidence.
Public value, historical operation, research gap, and six task deliverables.
Simulation assumptions and start of discrete right-most-rule modeling.
Particle-hopping representation, notation, and rule tables.
Parameters, metric curves, weighted speed selection, and CA visualization.
Single- and two-lane PDE construction, steady state, and numerical dynamics.
Cross-model comparison, orientation transfer, and alternative traffic rules.
Median controller, equipped comparisons, and online-control limitation.
Ordered recap of baseline, alternatives, and intelligent control.
References are excluded; the appendix C++ is retained for model/reproducibility evidence only.

contributions.summary: Pairs a microscopic particle-hopping CA with a macro-scale two-lane PDE.
Makes safety, Rule #0, and Rule #1 lane changes explicit.
Uses a declared weighted objective over flow, risk proxy, and energy proxy.
Reports shared unimodal density-flow behavior across CA and PDE.
Compares KRETP, SCTR, and FDFO through the same metric bundle.
Uses full-state median speed to balance lane preferences dynamically.
Supplies substantial C++ implementation evidence including repetitions and warm-up.

feedbacks: M3/M4 provide qualitative cross-model corroboration for M1, not external calibration.
Appendix code supports M1/M8 reproduction but does not fix missing scenario configuration.
dependency_graph.closure_status: Positive policy-to-model-to-decision routes are complete. Exact experimental reproduction remains limited by missing configuration files, seeds, figure pipelines, and source inconsistencies.

assumptions.summary: Automobiles move in straight lines on a freeway without extra entrances or exits.
Jams arise from gradual vehicle piling; sudden crashes are excluded.
Drivers obey rules, lane changes take no time, and vehicles share length and mass.
The freeway is a circular loop, preserving density.
Flow, safety proxy, and energy proxy are treated as independent terms in a simple weighted sum.
The two-lane system is asymmetric because of overtaking and driving roles.
The controller knows exact locations and velocities and can act on all vehicles.

data_and_preprocessing.summary: Defines model state and pre-evaluated parameters rather than using external observed traffic data.
Randomizes positions and speeds while preserving total density in two lanes.
States lattice length, duration, density sequence, probabilities, speed limits, and vehicle mixture.
Lists cited continuum parameters and equilibrium-speed settings.
Combines separate fast and slow lane outputs at 0.5 weights.
Reads missing coef.prn to override defaults, creating a reproducibility dependency.

MU-A-2014-29911-002: Select maximum velocity under light, heavy, and mixed density regimes.
MU-A-2014-29911-003: Represent density, velocity, relaxation, anticipation, and asymmetric lane exchange at macroscopic scale.

MU-A-2014-29911-006: Provide an unrestricted alternative to rightmost and speed-segregated rules.
MU-A-2014-29911-007: Compare baseline and counterfactual rules on aligned density-response metrics and derive a qualified recommendation.
MU-A-2014-29911-008: Use full traffic-state information to separate higher- and lower-speed vehicles dynamically.
MU-A-2014-29911-009: Describe how centralized information could coordinate vehicles trapped without a local gap.

verification.summary: Figures 3-5 show internal response patterns, not field calibration.
Figures 6-8 are within-model parameter scans supporting Vmax=5 under stated weights.
Figure 11 provides qualitative density-flow agreement with the CA.
Figures 12-14 illustrate regime-specific perturbation behavior under an externally cited numerical scheme.
Figures 15-17 compare three policies on the common metrics without uncertainty bands.
Figures 19-21 show modest equipped/not-equipped differences without published replication statistics.

results_trace.summary: CA flow increases at low density, peaks near the stated capacity regime, then declines under congestion.
The stated 4:1 mixed objective has its plotted maximum at Vmax=5.
PDE curves share the low-density increase and high-density decrease of CA flow.
FDFO is reported worse in light traffic while high-density curves converge.
The source recommends keeping KRETP and selectively separating fast/slow lanes on frequently congested freeways.
Median control is reported beneficial but not dramatic in the source's three metrics.

judge_relevance_hypotheses.summary: An ordered one-page route may aid traceability, but award status does not establish a judge preference.
A visible input-output procedure may help reviewability, but no judging evidence is supplied.
Aligned comparator plots may make a policy recommendation inspectable, not causally award-determining.

weaknesses.summary: The printed single-lane continuity equation differentiates u rather than rho, unlike the two-lane conservation form.
Source prose and net-inflow notation leave Sij direction semantics ambiguous.
Qe is defined with lane density then reused as a function of average density.
rho_h and Delta rho_h are not numerically defined.
The CA/PDE comparison points to Figure 9 rather than the Figure 11 flow-density curve.
Figures 12 and 13 list identical parameter rows despite different claimed initial-lane perturbations.
The claimed Wagner-derived rule is cited to a different textbook source.
The kinetic-energy simplification omits conditions needed for its displayed reduction.
Table 1 says per-lane flow while formula/code expose different aggregation conventions.
Appendix defaults differ from prose and actual overrides depend on missing coef.prn.
The code computes repeat standard deviations but paper figures report neither them nor seeds.
Coordinated queue release is conceptual rather than an implemented constrained optimizer.
Time-step and lattice-length calibration appear only as future work, so Vmax=5 cannot be directly treated as a real speed limit.

independent_extensions.summary: Publish coef.prn, source-controlled seeds, build commands, raw logs, and plot scripts; regenerate all figures with uncertainty bands.
Elicit or sweep stakeholder weights, test normalized value-function shapes, and report near-optimal speed sets rather than one nominal maximum.
Correct and dimension-check conservation equations, exchange direction, boundary/initial conditions, and numerical convergence.
Use paired common-random-number runs, publish confidence intervals, add enforcement/cost data, and test decision reversals.
Specify communications, actuation, latency, failure modes, controller code, and congestion-regime performance statistics.
Calibrate cell length, time step, vehicle heterogeneity, weather, sight distance, and external observed flow/safety data.
